questions.question: When the sun, the moon and the earth are in a straight line, the height of the tide will be higher. What are these tides called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Spring tides**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Spring tides occur when the sun, the moon, and the earth are in a straight line during the new moon and full moon phases.
 
• These tides are characterized by higher high tides and lower low tides due to the combined gravitational pull of the sun and the moon.
 
• The term "spring" does not refer to the season but rather the concept of "springing forth" in terms of increased tidal range.
 
• Spring tides happen approximately twice a month, during the full moon and new moon phases.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Neap tides:**

 
 
• Neap tides occur when the sun and moon are at right angles to each other (first and third quarters of the moon).
 
• These tides are characterized by a smaller tidal range, with lower high tides and higher low tides.
 
• The gravitational forces of the sun and the moon partially cancel each other out during neap tides.
 
 
 
• **Diurnal tide:**
 
 
• Diurnal tides refer to a tidal pattern with one high tide and one low tide each day.
 
• This type of tide is less common and typically occurs in certain geographical regions.
 
• Diurnal tides are found in areas such as the Gulf of Mexico and parts of Southeast Asia.
 
 
 
• **Gravitational forces:**
 
 
• The gravitational pull of the moon and the sun affects the Earth's water, causing tides.
 
• The moon has a greater influence on tides due to its proximity to Earth compared to the sun.
 
• Tides are the periodic rise and fall of sea levels caused by the combined effects of gravitational forces exerted by the moon, the sun, and the rotation of the Earth.

questions.question: Bhangra dance is commonly performed in which of these states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Punjab**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bhangra** is a lively form of folk music and dance that originated in the **Punjab region of India**.
 
• It is traditionally performed during the **harvest season** and at various celebrations such as weddings and festivals.
 
• The dance is known for its **vigorous movements and energetic beats** performed to the rhythm of dhol, a type of drum.
 
• Bhangra has gained international popularity and is often featured in **Bollywood movies** and other cultural events around the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Punjab**

 
 
• Punjab is a state in northern India known for its rich culture, vibrant festivals, and historical significance.
 
• The state is divided into two parts: East Punjab in India and West Punjab in Pakistan, after the partition in 1947.
 
• Punjab is often referred to as the "Granary of India" or "India's Bread Basket" due to its fertile soil and extensive agricultural production.
 
• Punjabi cuisine is famous for its rich and spicy flavors, with dishes like butter chicken, sarson da saag, and makki di roti being popular worldwide.
 
 
 
• **Bhangra Music**
 
 
• Bhangra music is characterized by its upbeat tempo and use of traditional instruments such as the dhol, tumbi, and chimta.
 
• The lyrics of Bhangra songs often revolve around themes of love, patriotism, and social issues.
 
• Modern Bhangra has evolved to incorporate elements of hip-hop, reggae, and electronic music, making it popular among younger generations.
 
• Popular Bhangra artists include Gurdas Maan, Daler Mehndi, and Jazzy B.
 
 
 
• **Harvest Festivals in Punjab**
 
 
• Baisakhi is one of the most significant harvest festivals celebrated in Punjab, marking the beginning of the new harvest season.
 
• The festival is celebrated with great enthusiasm and includes traditional Bhangra and Gidda performances, fairs, and community feasts.
 
• Other important festivals in Punjab include Lohri, which marks the end of winter, and Maghi, which celebrates the winter harvest.
 
• These festivals reflect the agrarian lifestyle and cultural richness of the Punjabi people.

questions.question: The goal of Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana was to develop _________ Adarsh Grams by March 2019.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**three**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The goal of Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana (SAGY) is to develop model villages (Adarsh Grams) through the adoption of existing ones by Members of Parliament (MPs).
 
• Each MP is required to develop three Adarsh Grams by March 2019, of which one should be achieved by 2016 and the other two by 2019.
 
• The scheme was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 11th October 2014 on the birth anniversary of Lok Nayak Jai Prakash Narayan.
 
• The aim is to translate Gandhiji's vision of an ideal Indian village into reality, focusing on holistic development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana (SAGY)**

 
 
• SAGY is a rural development program broadly focusing on the development of villages, including social development, cultural development, and motivating the community to take the lead in local development.
 
• Under the scheme, Members of Parliament will be responsible for developing the socio-economic and physical infrastructure of three villages by 2019 and eight villages by 2024.
 
• The key components of SAGY include participatory planning, convergence, and implementation of various government schemes and programs, leading to comprehensive village development.
 
• The scheme emphasizes the empowerment of women, youth, and marginalized sections, and seeks to provide basic amenities, quality education, health services, sanitation, and skill development.
 
 
 
• **Other Government Schemes for Rural Development**
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana - Gramin (PMAY-G):**
 
 
• Launched in 2016, PMAY-G aims to provide "Housing for All" by 2022 by building pucca houses with basic amenities for the homeless and those living in kutcha houses.
 
 
 
• **Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (DDUGJY):**
 
 
• Launched in 2015, DDUGJY focuses on rural electrification and providing continuous power supply to rural India.
 
 
 
• **Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin):**
 
 
• Launched in 2014, it aims to eliminate open defecation and improve solid waste management in rural areas.

questions.question: Which of the following architectural features/structures was NOT a part of the citadel in Mohenjo-Daro?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Residential Buildings**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The citadel of Mohenjo-Daro was a fortified area that contained various important structures.
 
• The Great Bath was one of the most famous structures found on the citadel, used for ritual bathing.
 
• Other key structures included the Great Granary, which served as a warehouse for storing grain.
 
• Additionally, the citadel had a Pillared Hall, which may have been used for administrative or ceremonial purposes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mohenjo-Daro:**

 
 
• Mohenjo-Daro, meaning "Mound of the Dead Men," is an archaeological site in the province of Sindh, Pakistan.
 
• It was one of the largest settlements of the ancient Indus Valley Civilization, built around 2500 BCE.
 
• The site was designated a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1980.
 
 
 
• **Great Bath:**
 
 
• The Great Bath is one of the most remarkable structures in Mohenjo-Daro.
 
• It measures approximately 12 meters long, 7 meters wide, and 2.4 meters deep.
 
• It is believed to have been used for ritualistic purposes, possibly for religious ceremonies.
 
 
 
• **Great Granary:**
 
 
• The Great Granary is one of the largest structures in Mohenjo-Daro.
 
• It was used for the storage of surplus grain, which indicates an organized approach to agriculture and food distribution.
 
 
 
• **Pillared Hall:**
 
 
• The Pillared Hall is another significant structure found on the citadel.
 
• It is believed to have been used for administrative or ceremonial functions.
 
• The hall contained several pillars, which may have supported a roof, indicating advanced architectural knowledge.

questions.question: Posthumus Padma awardee in 2022, Gosaveedu Shalik Hassan was a renowned player of the _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nadaswaram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Gosaveedu Shalik Hassan was a celebrated player of the Nadaswaram, a traditional Indian musical instrument.
 
• He was posthumously awarded the Padma Shri in 2022 for his contributions to Indian classical music.
 
• Nadaswaram is a wind instrument, often referred to as the world's loudest non-brass acoustic instrument.
 
• It is commonly played in South Indian classical music, especially during temple festivals and weddings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Padma Awards**

 
 
• Padma Awards are one of the highest civilian honors in India, instituted in the year 1954.
 
• They are given in three categories: Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, and Padma Shri, in decreasing order of precedence.
 
• The awards are given in various disciplines/fields of activities, including art, social work, public affairs, science and engineering, trade and industry, medicine, literature and education, sports, and civil service.
 
 
 
• **Indian Classical Music**
 
 
• Indian classical music is divided into two major traditions: Hindustani (North Indian) and Carnatic (South Indian).
 
• Nadaswaram is predominantly used in Carnatic music.
 
• It is often accompanied by another instrument called "Thavil", a type of drum.
 
 
 
• **Traditional Indian Instruments**
 
 
• India has a rich tradition of music with a variety of instruments like Sitar, Veena, Tabla, Mridangam, and more.
 
• Each instrument has its unique sound and playing technique, deeply rooted in the cultural and religious practices of the region.

questions.question: In Karate, which word is used to denote ‘Punch’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tsuki**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In Karate, the term **Tsuki** refers to a punch or thrusting technique.
 
• Tsuki is fundamental in Karate and is used to strike an opponent effectively using the fist.
 
• This technique involves precise body mechanics, including the rotation of the hips and shoulders to generate power.
 
• Practitioners often train Tsuki in various stances to improve accuracy, speed, and power.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Waza-ari**

 
 
• Waza-ari is a term used in martial arts like Judo and Karate to signify a half-point score.
 
• It indicates a technique that was performed well but not perfectly, thereby earning a half-point.
 
• In Karate competitions, accumulating two Waza-aris can lead to an Ippon, which is a full point.
 
 
 
• **Seiri**
 
 
• Seiri is a Japanese term generally referring to order or organization.
 
• In the context of Karate, it is not commonly used to denote any specific technique or term.
 
 
 
• **Ippon**
 
 
• Ippon is a term used in martial arts to denote a full point.
 
• In Karate, an Ippon is awarded for a technique that is executed with perfect form, power, and timing, demonstrating full control and effectiveness.
 
• Achieving an Ippon can immediately decide the outcome of a match in favor of the one who scores it.

questions.question: Which of the following fungus is used in fermentation technology?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Saccharomyces**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Saccharomyces** is a genus of fungi that includes many species of yeasts.
 
• The most well-known species is **Saccharomyces cerevisiae**, which is used in baking, brewing, and winemaking.
 
• **Saccharomyces cerevisiae** is known as baker's yeast or brewer's yeast and plays a crucial role in fermentation.
 
• This yeast converts carbohydrates to carbon dioxide and alcohols, a process that is essential in bread making and alcohol production.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fermentation Technology:**

 
 
• Fermentation is a metabolic process that produces chemical changes in organic substrates through the action of enzymes.
 
• In the context of food and drink, fermentation refers to the process by which yeast and bacteria convert sugars into alcohol, gases, or acids.
 
• Fermentation is used in various applications, including the production of beer, wine, bread, yogurt, and other fermented foods.
 
• It is an anaerobic process, meaning it occurs in the absence of oxygen.
 
 
 
• **Rhizobium:**
 
 
• Rhizobium is a genus of bacteria that fix nitrogen after becoming established inside the root nodules of legumes.
 
• They are not involved in fermentation but play a crucial role in soil fertility and agriculture.
 
 
 
• **Molds:**
 
 
• Molds are fungi that grow in the form of multicellular filaments called hyphae.
 
• They are used in the production of certain foods like cheese (e.g., Penicillium species in blue cheese) but are not primarily used in fermentation technology.
 
 
 
• **Smuts:**
 
 
• Smuts are fungi that affect grains and grasses, causing plant diseases.
 
• They are not used in fermentation but are significant in agriculture due to their impact on crops.

questions.question: As per Article 170 of the Constitution of India, the Legislative Assembly of each State shall consist of NOT more than ____________and not less than 60 members.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**500**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 170 of the Constitution of India deals with the composition of the Legislative Assemblies of States.
 
• The Legislative Assembly of each State shall consist of not more than 500 and not less than 60 members.
 
• This limitation ensures that the size of the Legislative Assembly is manageable and can effectively represent the population of the state.
 
• There are exceptions to this rule, such as in the cases of smaller states like Sikkim, which have fewer than 60 members due to their smaller population.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Legislative Assembly:**

 
 
• Also known as Vidhan Sabha, it is the lower house of the state legislature in India.
 
• Members of the Legislative Assembly (MLAs) are directly elected by the people of the state.
 
• The term of the Legislative Assembly is five years, unless dissolved sooner.
 
• The Assembly is responsible for making laws on subjects enumerated in the State List of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Article 170:**
 
 
• This article of the Indian Constitution specifies the composition of the Legislative Assemblies of States.
 
• It sets the maximum and minimum limits for the number of members in a state's Legislative Assembly.
 
• The size of each Legislative Assembly is based on the population of the state as per the last Census.
 
 
 
• **Exceptions:**
 
 
• Some states with smaller populations, such as Sikkim, Goa, and Mizoram, have Legislative Assemblies with fewer than 60 members.
 
• These exceptions are made to accommodate the unique demographic and geographic characteristics of these states.
 
 
 
• **State List:**
 
 
• The State List is a list of subjects under the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India.
 
• It enumerates the areas in which only the state governments can legislate.
 
• Examples of subjects in the State List include police, public health, and agriculture.

questions.question: Which of the following elements is NOT related to the Trade and Investment Policy Reforms?

options.text: Dismantling of quantitative restrictions on imports and exports

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Increase in export duties**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Trade and Investment Policy Reforms typically aim to promote trade and investment flows by reducing restrictions and barriers.
 
• Dismantling of quantitative restrictions on imports and exports promotes free trade by removing limits on the quantity of goods that can be traded.
 
• Reduction of tariff rates lowers the cost of imported goods, making trade more feasible and competitive.
 
• Removal of licensing for imports simplifies the process of importing goods, making it easier for businesses to engage in trade.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dismantling of quantitative restrictions on imports and exports:**

 
 
• Quantitative restrictions refer to limits on the quantity of goods that can be imported or exported. Removing these restrictions encourages more open and competitive markets.
 
• This step is crucial for integrating a country's economy with the global market and can lead to increased trade volumes.
 
 
 
• **Reduction of tariff rates:**
 
 
• Tariffs are taxes imposed on imported goods. Reducing tariff rates makes imported goods cheaper, encouraging trade and competition.
 
• Lower tariffs can also benefit consumers by providing them with a wider variety of goods at lower prices.
 
 
 
• **Removal of licensing for imports:**
 
 
• Licensing requirements can act as barriers to trade by making the process of importing goods complex and time-consuming.
 
• Removing licensing requirements simplifies the import process, encouraging businesses to engage in international trade.
 
 
 
• **Increase in export duties:**
 
 
• Export duties are taxes imposed on goods being sent out of a country. Increasing export duties can make a country's goods more expensive and less competitive in the international market.
 
• While the other measures aim to facilitate trade, increasing export duties does the opposite by creating additional costs for exporters.

questions.question: The process of privatisation covers three sets of measures. Which of the following is NOT one of those?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Accounting measures**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Privatisation involves transferring ownership, management, and control of public sector enterprises to the private sector.
 
• The three main measures of privatisation are Ownership measures, Operational measures, and Organisational measures.
 
• Ownership measures include selling public sector equity to private entities.
 
• Operational measures focus on improving efficiency through better management practices, while Organisational measures involve restructuring the organization to enhance performance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ownership Measures**

 
 
• These measures include the complete or partial sale of government-owned enterprises to private entities.
 
• They aim to reduce the financial burden on the government and improve the efficiency of enterprises through private sector management.
 
 
 
• **Operational Measures**
 
 
• Operational measures focus on enhancing the efficiency and productivity of enterprises.
 
• This can include the adoption of new technologies, better management practices, and employee training programs.
 
 
 
• **Organisational Measures**
 
 
• Organisational measures involve restructuring the enterprise to make it more efficient.
 
• This can include decentralization, reducing layers of management, and creating more flexible structures.
 
 
 
• **Privatisation**
 
 
• Privatisation is the process of transferring ownership and management of enterprises from the public sector to the private sector.

questions.question: The author of Prayag Prashasti, Harisena, was the court poet of whom among the following Gupta rulers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Samudragupta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Harisena was a renowned poet and scholar in the court of the Gupta emperor **Samudragupta**.
 
• The Prayag Prashasti, also known as the **Allahabad Pillar Inscription**, was composed by Harisena.
 
• The inscription is an important source of historical information about the reign and accomplishments of Samudragupta.
 
• It provides a detailed account of Samudragupta's military campaigns, conquests, and his skills as a ruler and administrator.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prayag Prashasti**

 
 
• The Prayag Prashasti is an inscription found on the Allahabad Pillar, which was originally erected by Ashoka, the Mauryan emperor, and later inscribed by Samudragupta.
 
• It is written in classical Sanskrit and is composed in the form of a eulogy or prashasti.
 
• The inscription highlights Samudragupta's victories over various kings and his establishment of a vast empire.
 
• It also mentions his patronage of arts and culture, portraying him as a versatile and benevolent ruler.
 
 
 
• **Samudragupta**
 
 
• Samudragupta was one of the greatest rulers of the Gupta Empire, often referred to as the "Napoleon of India" for his extensive military campaigns and conquests.
 
• He ruled from approximately 335 to 375 CE and was known for his administrative skills, cultural patronage, and military prowess.
 
• His reign marked a golden age of art, literature, and science in ancient India.
 
• Samudragupta's achievements are celebrated in various historical records and inscriptions, with the Prayag Prashasti being one of the most significant.
 
 
 
• **Gupta Empire**
 
 
• The Gupta Empire, which lasted from around 320 to 550 CE, is considered a classical period in Indian history, known for its advancements in arts, science, and political administration.
 
• It was established by Sri Gupta and reached its zenith under rulers like Chandragupta I, Samudragupta, and Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya).
 
• The period saw the flourishing of classical Sanskrit literature, significant developments in mathematics and astronomy, and the creation of magnificent art and architecture.
 
• The decline of the Gupta Empire began in the late 5th century, eventually leading to its fall due to invasions and internal conflicts.

questions.question: In medieval architecture, Sarais are places used for _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**temporary accommodation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Sarais were essentially inns or rest houses established in medieval times.
 
• They provided temporary accommodation for travelers, merchants, and pilgrims.
 
• These structures were often found along trade routes and were crucial for the safety and comfort of travelers.
 
• Sarais typically included facilities like rooms for sleeping, stables for animals, and sometimes even food provisions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Medieval Architecture**

 
 
• Medieval architecture refers to the architectural styles that were prevalent in Europe during the Middle Ages, roughly from the 5th to the late 15th century.
 
• It includes a variety of styles such as Romanesque, Gothic, and Byzantine.
 
• Key features of medieval architecture include the use of stone, pointed arches, ribbed vaults, and flying buttresses.
 
• Buildings from this period include castles, churches, and fortifications, all serving different purposes from defense to religious worship.
 
 
 
• **Trade Routes**
 
 
• Trade routes were essential pathways used for the commercial movement of goods and services.
 
• They facilitated the exchange of commodities like spices, silk, precious metals, and other goods between different regions.
 
• Famous medieval trade routes include the Silk Road, the Amber Road, and the Trans-Saharan trade routes.
 
• These routes not only boosted economic activity but also enabled cultural and technological exchanges between civilizations.
 
 
 
• **Hospices and Inns**
 
 
• Similar to sarais, hospices and inns were established to offer lodging and care for travelers and pilgrims.
 
• Hospices, often run by religious institutions, provided free or low-cost shelter and food to the needy and the sick.
 
• Inns were more commercial establishments that charged for lodging and meals, catering mainly to merchants and other travelers.
 
• These facilities played a significant role in medieval society by promoting travel and commerce.

questions.question: Which country is the host of the 2023 ODI Cricket World Cup event?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India is hosting the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2023 for the fourth time. The previous years were 1987, 1996, and 2011.
 
• This will be the 13th edition of the Men's Cricket World Cup, organized by the International Cricket Council (ICC).
 
• The tournament is expected to feature 10 teams from around the world, competing over several weeks for the prestigious trophy.
 
• India has previously won the Cricket World Cup twice, in 1983 under the captaincy of Kapil Dev and in 2011 under the captaincy of MS Dhoni.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **ICC (International Cricket Council)**

 
 
• The ICC is the global governing body for cricket, responsible for the organization and governance of cricket's major international tournaments.
 
• It was founded as the Imperial Cricket Conference in 1909 by representatives from England, Australia, and South Africa.
 
• The ICC has 104 member countries, including 12 full members that play Test matches and 92 associate members.
 
 
 
• **Cricket World Cup**
 
 
• The Cricket World Cup is an international championship of One Day International (ODI) cricket.
 
• The event is organized by the sport's governing body, the ICC, every four years.
 
• The first Cricket World Cup was held in England in 1975, and since then, it has grown to become one of the most watched sporting events globally.
 
• The tournament format has evolved over the years, with the current format featuring a round-robin group stage followed by knockout rounds.
 
 
 
• **One Day International (ODI)**
 
 
• An ODI is a form of limited-overs cricket, played between two teams with international status.
 
• Each team faces a set number of overs, usually 50, and the team that scores the most runs wins the match.
 
• ODIs are recognized for their exciting and fast-paced nature, as compared to Test matches, which can last up to five days.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT about the an earthquake?

options.text: An earthquake is shaking of the earth.
An earthquake is caused due to release of energy.
An earthquake is a natural event.
An earthquake creates waves that spread in one direction.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4: An earthquake creates waves that spread in one direction.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• An earthquake is the shaking of the earth's surface caused by the sudden release of energy in the Earth's lithosphere.
 
• This energy release creates seismic waves that propagate in all directions, not just one.
 
• Earthquakes are natural events and can be caused by tectonic movements, volcanic activity, and other geological processes.
 
• The point inside the Earth where the earthquake starts is called the focus or hypocenter, and the point directly above it on the surface is the epicenter.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Seismic Waves:**

 
 
• Seismic waves are the waves of energy that travel through the Earth's layers and are a result of an earthquake, volcanic eruption, magma movement, large landslides, and large man-made explosions that give out low-frequency acoustic energy.
 
• There are two main types of seismic waves: body waves and surface waves. Body waves travel through the Earth's interior, while surface waves travel along the Earth's surface.
 
• Body waves are further divided into Primary (P) waves, which are compressional waves, and Secondary (S) waves, which are shear waves.
 
 
 
• **Richter Scale:**
 
 
• The Richter scale is a logarithmic scale used to measure the magnitude of an earthquake. It quantifies the amount of energy released by an earthquake.
 
• A higher magnitude on the Richter scale indicates a more powerful earthquake.
 
 
 
• **Aftershocks:**
 
 
• Aftershocks are smaller earthquakes that follow the main shock of a larger earthquake.
 
• They can continue over a period of weeks, months, or even years after the initial earthquake event.
 
 
 
• **Tectonic Plates:**
 
 
• The Earth's lithosphere is divided into several large and small pieces called tectonic plates.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution mentions that ‘Untouchability’ is abolished and its practice in any form is forbidden?

• **Untouchability**

 
 
• Untouchability is a social practice in India that ostracizes a certain section of the community, particularly the Dalits, by considering them impure and polluting.
 
• This practice has its roots in the caste system, which divides society into hierarchical groups based on occupation and birth.
 
• The practice of untouchability leads to severe social discrimination, economic exploitation, and denial of basic rights and dignity.
 
• Article 17 aims to eliminate this practice and promote social justice and equality among all citizens.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Rights**
 
 
• Fundamental Rights are a set of rights granted to all citizens of India by the Constitution.
 
• These rights are considered essential for the development of the individual and the nation.
 
• They include rights such as the right to equality, freedom of speech, freedom of religion, cultural and educational rights, and the right to constitutional remedies.
 
• These rights are enforceable by the courts, and any violation can be challenged in a court of law.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Provisions**

• It was adopted on 26th November 1949 and came into effect on 26th January 1950.
 
• The Constitution consists of a Preamble, 448 Articles, 25 Parts, and 12 Schedules.
 
• It lays down the principles of democracy, justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity.
 
 
 
• **Legal Provisions**

• The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955, prohibits the practice of untouchability and prescribes penalties for its violation.
 
• The Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, provides stringent measures to prevent atrocities against these communities.
 
• These legal provisions aim to ensure the effective implementation of the constitutional mandate against untouchability.

• **Varna System:**

 
 
• The Varna system is a traditional division of Hindu society into four main categories: Brahmins (priests and teachers), Kshatriyas (warriors and rulers), Vaisyas (traders and agriculturists), and Shudras (laborers and service providers).
 
• This social stratification is based on ancient Hindu scriptures and has played a significant role in the social organization of Indian society.

• The Gupta Empire was an ancient Indian empire that existed from approximately 320 to 550 CE.
 
• Founded by Maharaja Sri Gupta, the dynasty is noted for its significant contributions to various fields including literature, science, art, and architecture.
 
• During the Gupta period, India witnessed a flourishing of culture, prosperity, and intellectual achievements, often referred to as the Golden Age of India.
 
• Famous rulers of the Gupta Dynasty include Chandragupta I, Samudragupta, and Chandragupta II (also known as Chandragupta Vikramaditya).
 
 
 
• **Golden Age of India:**
 
 
• The term "Golden Age of India" refers to a period of great cultural and economic prosperity in Indian history.
 
• The Gupta Empire is particularly known for this era due to its advancements in various fields such as mathematics (concept of zero), astronomy, medicine, literature, and art.
 
• Famous scholars such as Kalidasa and Aryabhata emerged during this period, contributing significantly to the cultural and scientific heritage of India.

• The celebration of Ganesh Chaturthi was revived by Bal Gangadhar Tilak in the late 19th century to unite Indians against British rule.
 
• The festival involves the installation of Ganesha idols in homes and public places, followed by prayers, cultural performances, and processions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Shivaji is known for his innovative military tactics, guerrilla warfare, and strong naval presence.
 
 
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak:**

• Tilak revived the celebration of Ganesh Chaturthi to build a sense of unity and nationalism among Indians during British rule.
 
 
 
• **Ganesh Chaturthi Celebrations:**

questions.question: Which is the highest court of appeal in India?

__
 
• The Supreme Court of India is the highest judicial forum and final court of appeal under the Constitution of India.
 
• It was established on January 28, 1950, two days after India became a republic.
 
• The Supreme Court comprises the Chief Justice of India and a maximum of 33 other judges.
 
• It has extensive powers in the form of original, appellate and advisory jurisdictions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lok Adalat:**

 
 
• Also known as "People's Court," it is a system of alternative dispute resolution developed in India.
 
• It is a forum where disputes/cases pending in the court of law or at pre-litigation stage are settled/compromised amicably.
 
• The Lok Adalat has been given statutory status under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.
 
• Lok Adalats are organized by the State Legal Services Authority or District Legal Services Authority.
 
 
 
• **District Court:**
 
 
• The District Courts of India are established by the State governments of India for every district or for one or more districts together taking into account the number of cases, population distribution, etc.
 
• These courts are under the administrative control of the High Court of the State to which the district concerned belongs.
 
• The District Court is responsible for both civil and criminal matters within the district.
 
• It is the principal court of original jurisdiction and can also act as an appellate court.
 
 
 
• **High Court:**
 
 
• The High Courts of India are the principal civil courts of original jurisdiction in each state and union territory.
 
• However, a High Court exercises its original civil and criminal jurisdiction only if the subordinate courts are not competent to try the matters.
 
• High Courts also have appellate jurisdiction over the lower courts and tribunals within their jurisdiction.
 
• There are 25 High Courts in India as of now.
 
 
 
• **Supreme Court of India:**
 
 
• The Supreme Court is the apex court in the judicial hierarchy of India.
 
• It has a wide range of powers and its decisions are binding on all other courts in the country.
 
• The court's primary role is to interpret the Constitution and laws passed by Parliament and state legislatures.
 
• It also has the power to hear appeals from lower courts and can issue writs to enforce fundamental rights.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Mitochondria is INCORRECT?

options.text: ATP generating chemical reactions get enhanced by the deeply folded surface area of the mitochondria.
The body uses energy stored in ATP for making new chemical compounds and for mechanical work.
Mitochondria are not capable of making their own proteins.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mitochondria are not capable of making their own proteins**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mitochondria are indeed capable of making their own proteins.** They contain their own DNA and ribosomes which allow them to synthesize certain proteins independently.
 
• The mitochondrial inner membrane is extensively folded into structures known as cristae, which increase the surface area available for ATP-generating chemical reactions.
 
• The energy stored in ATP is used by the body for various processes, including the synthesis of new chemical compounds and mechanical work.
 
• **Mitochondria have a double-membrane structure.** The outer membrane is smooth, while the inner membrane is folded into cristae.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mitochondria**

 
 
• Mitochondria are known as the powerhouses of the cell because they generate most of the cell's supply of ATP, used as a source of chemical energy.
 
• They are unique in having their own genome, which is similar to bacterial genomes, and they reproduce independently of the cell in which they reside.
 
• The double-membrane structure of mitochondria consists of an outer membrane and a highly convoluted inner membrane, the latter being the site of the electron transport chain and ATP synthesis.
 
• The inner membrane folds over many times to create layered structures called cristae. The increased surface area of these cristae enhances the mitochondrion's ability to produce ATP.
 
 
 
• **ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate)**
 
 
• ATP is the energy currency of the cell, providing the energy needed for many biochemical cellular processes including muscle contraction and protein synthesis.
 
• It is produced primarily in the mitochondria through a process known as oxidative phosphorylation, which occurs along the inner mitochondrial membrane.
 
 
 
• **Protein Synthesis in Mitochondria**
 
 
• Mitochondria have their own ribosomes and DNA, which enable them to produce some of their own proteins independently of the cell's nuclear DNA.
 
• The mitochondrial DNA encodes for a small number of proteins essential for the organelle’s function, particularly those involved in the electron transport chain.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Climate Resilience**

 
 
• Climate resilience refers to the ability of a system, community, or environment to cope with and adapt to changing climatic conditions, such as extreme weather events, rising temperatures, and altered precipitation patterns.
 
• In agriculture, developing climate-resilient crop varieties is crucial to ensure stable food production even under adverse climatic conditions.
 
 
 
• **High Nutrient Content**
 
 
• Crops with high nutrient content are bred to have elevated levels of essential vitamins, minerals, and other nutrients.
 
• This biofortification process aims to address malnutrition and improve the overall nutritional status of the population consuming these crops.
 
 
 
• **Food Security**
 
 
• Food security means ensuring that all people at all times have physical, social, and economic access to sufficient, safe, and nutritious food that meets their dietary needs and food preferences for an active and healthy life.
 
• Developing and promoting crop varieties with special traits, such as climate resilience and high nutrient content, plays a key role in achieving food security.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Agriculture**
 
 
• Sustainable agriculture involves farming practices that meet current food needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their needs.
 
• It encompasses techniques that protect the environment, public health, human communities, and animal welfare.
 
• The introduction of crop varieties with special traits supports sustainable agriculture by enhancing productivity and resilience while minimizing environmental impact.

questions.question: The Gangaur festival of Rajasthan starts and ends on which days as per the Hindu calendar?

options.text: First day of Phalguna (Krishna)-Third day of Phalguna (Shukla)
First day of Jyeshtha (Krishna)-Third day of Jyeshtha (Shukla)
First day of Ashadh (Krishna)-Third day of Ashadh (Shukla)
First day of Chaitra (Krishna)-Third day of Chaitra (Shukla)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**First day of Chaitra (Krishna) - Third day of Chaitra (Shukla)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Gangaur festival is a significant and colorful festival celebrated in the Indian state of Rajasthan.
 
• It starts on the first day of Chaitra (Krishna Paksha) and ends on the third day of Chaitra (Shukla Paksha) as per the Hindu calendar.
 
• This festival is dedicated to Gauri, a manifestation of Goddess Parvati, who represents marital bliss and conjugal happiness.
 
• Women worship Gauri for the long life, health, and prosperity of their husbands and family members.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chaitra Month:**

 
 
• Chaitra is the first month of the Hindu lunar calendar. It typically falls in March-April of the Gregorian calendar.
 
• The month marks the arrival of spring and the start of the New Year in several traditional Indian calendars.
 
 
 
• **Krishna Paksha:**
 
 
• Krishna Paksha refers to the waning phase of the moon, which is the 15-day period from the full moon to the new moon.
 
• This period is considered auspicious for performing certain rituals and festivals in Hinduism.
 
 
 
• **Shukla Paksha:**
 
 
• Shukla Paksha refers to the waxing phase of the moon, which is the 15-day period from the new moon to the full moon.
 
• Many festivals and religious events are celebrated during this bright fortnight.
 
 
 
• **Gauri (Parvati):**
 
 
• Gauri is another name for Goddess Parvati, the consort of Lord Shiva.
 
• She symbolizes purity, fertility, and marital bliss and is revered especially by married women.

questions.question: Which of the following refers to ‘net indirect taxes’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indirect taxes - subsidies**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• 'Net indirect taxes' refer to the total amount of indirect taxes collected by the government after subtracting the subsidies provided.
 
• Indirect taxes are taxes that are not directly paid by the individual, such as sales tax, VAT, excise duty, etc.
 
• Subsidies are financial support provided by the government to reduce the cost of goods and services, making them more affordable for consumers.
 
• The formula for net indirect taxes is: **Net Indirect Taxes = Indirect Taxes - Subsidies**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indirect Taxes**

 
 
• Indirect taxes are those taxes that are imposed on goods and services rather than on income or profits.
 
• Examples of indirect taxes include Goods and Services Tax (GST), excise duties, customs duties, and Value Added Tax (VAT).
 
• These taxes are typically included in the price of goods and services and are paid by the consumer.
 
 
 
• **Subsidies**
 
 
• Subsidies are financial aids provided by the government to support businesses, reduce the prices of essential goods, and encourage production.
 
• They can take various forms such as direct cash transfers, tax reductions, or price controls.
 
• Subsidies aim to make essential goods and services more affordable and to stimulate economic activity.
 
 
 
• **Net Indirect Taxes**
 
 
• The concept of net indirect taxes is important in national accounting and public finance.
 
• It helps in calculating the real revenue from indirect taxes after accounting for the cost of subsidies.
 
• This figure is crucial for understanding the net impact of tax policies on the economy.
 
 
 
• **Impact on GDP**
 
 
• Net indirect taxes are part of the calculation of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) using the expenditure method.
 
• In this method, GDP is calculated as the sum of consumption, investment, government spending, and net exports, adjusted for net indirect taxes.
 
• Understanding net indirect taxes is essential for accurate economic analysis and policy formulation.

questions.question: Which river in the Himalayas flows parallel to the Ganga as a right-bank tributary?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Yamuna**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Yamuna is the second-largest tributary river of the Ganga (Ganges) in northern India and flows parallel to it.
 
• Originating from the Yamunotri Glacier at a height of about 6,387 meters (20,955 ft) on the southwestern slopes of Banderpooch peaks in the Lower Himalayas in Uttarakhand, the Yamuna travels a total length of 1,376 kilometers (855 mi).
 
• The Yamuna River merges with the Ganges at Triveni Sangam, Prayagraj (Allahabad), which is a holy confluence in Hinduism.
 
• The Yamuna is a right-bank tributary of the Ganges, meaning it joins the Ganges from the right side when facing downstream.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ganga River**

 
 
• The Ganges, known as the Ganga in India, is the most sacred river to Hindus. It is worshipped as the goddess Ganga in Hinduism.
 
• The river originates from the Gangotri Glacier in the Indian state of Uttarakhand, and it flows through the states of Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, and West Bengal before emptying into the Bay of Bengal.
 
 
 
• **Ghaghara River**
 
 
• The Ghaghara, also known as Karnali, is a major left-bank tributary of the Ganges. It originates from the Tibetan Plateau near Lake Mansarovar.
 
• The Ghaghara joins the Ganges near Chhapra in the Indian state of Bihar.
 
 
 
• **Gandak River**
 
 
• The Gandak, also known as the Narayani in Nepal, is another left-bank tributary of the Ganges. It originates from the Nepal Himalayas.
 
• The river flows into India and merges with the Ganges near Hajipur in Bihar.
 
 
 
• **Kosi River**
 
 
• The Kosi River is known as the Sorrow of Bihar due to its frequent flooding. It is a left-bank tributary of the Ganges.
 
• The river originates from the Tibet region and flows through Nepal before entering India and joining the Ganges near Kursela in Bihar.

questions.question: As per census 2011, which of the following states recorded the lowest female literacy rate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajasthan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As per Census 2011, Rajasthan recorded the lowest female literacy rate among Indian states.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Census**

 
 
• The Census is a systematic and official count of a country's population, typically recording various details such as age, gender, occupation, and educational status.
 
• In India, the Census is conducted every ten years by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
 
 
 
• **Literacy Rate**
 
 
• The literacy rate is the percentage of people aged 7 and above who can read and write with understanding.
 
• It is a key indicator of educational attainment and is used to measure the educational level of the population.
 
 
 
• **Female Literacy Rate**
 
 
• This specific metric measures the literacy rate among females aged 7 and above.
 
• Female literacy is a crucial factor for social and economic development, influencing areas such as health, family planning, and economic productivity.

• The state government has implemented various programs like the Rajasthan Literacy Mission and the Rajiv Gandhi Scheme for Empowerment of Adolescent Girls (SABLA).

questions.question: Articles 36-51 of the Constitution of India pertain to ______________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Directive Principles of State Policy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are laid down in Part IV of the Constitution of India, from Articles 36 to 51.
 
• DPSPs are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government. These are not enforceable by any court, but the principles laid down therein are considered fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• These principles aim to create social and economic conditions under which the citizens can lead a good life.
 
• The DPSPs are inspired by the Directive Principles given in the Constitution of Ireland and also by the principles of Gandhism, socialism, and the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Duties:**

 
 
• These are defined as the moral obligations of all citizens to help promote a spirit of patriotism and to uphold the unity of India.
 
• They are listed in Part IV-A of the Indian Constitution, added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.
 
• There are 11 Fundamental Duties mentioned in Article 51A of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Rights:**
 
 
• These are the basic human rights enshrined in the Constitution of India which are guaranteed to all citizens.
 
• These rights are enforceable by the courts, subject to certain restrictions.
 
• They are included in Part III of the Constitution, from Articles 12 to 35.
 
 
 
• **The Union:**
 
 
• This refers to the Union Government or the central government of India.
 
• Part V of the Indian Constitution deals with the Union, which includes the executive, legislature, and judiciary at the central level.
 
• Articles 52 to 151 cover the Union Government.

questions.question: Who among the following was the founder of Al-Hilal newspaper during British India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maulana Abul Kalam Azad**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Maulana Abul Kalam Azad** was an Indian scholar and senior leader of the Indian National Congress during the Indian independence movement.
 
• He was one of the prominent leaders who actively participated in the freedom struggle against British rule.
 
• Maulana Abul Kalam Azad founded the newspaper **Al-Hilal** in 1912 to propagate the message of freedom and unity among Indians.
 
• He used **Al-Hilal** as a platform to criticize British policies and to advocate for the rights of Indians, particularly Muslims, during British rule in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Al-Hilal Newspaper**

 
 
• **Al-Hilal** was a weekly Urdu language newspaper established by Maulana Abul Kalam Azad in 1912.
 
• The newspaper played a significant role in spreading nationalist ideas and mobilizing public opinion against British colonial rule.
 
• Al-Hilal was known for its bold and fearless journalism, often criticizing the policies of the British government.
 
• The British authorities eventually banned **Al-Hilal** in 1914 due to its revolutionary and anti-colonial content.
 
 
 
• **Maulana Abul Kalam Azad**
 
 
• He was a prominent freedom fighter, Islamic theologian, and a senior leader of the Indian National Congress.
 
• Azad was known for his efforts in promoting Hindu-Muslim unity and was a staunch advocate of secularism.
 
• He served as India's first Minister of Education after independence and played a key role in shaping the country's educational policies.
 
• Azad was posthumously awarded the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award, in 1992.
 
 
 
• **British India**
 
 
• British India refers to the period of British colonial rule on the Indian subcontinent from 1858 to 1947.
 
• During this period, India was governed by the British Crown through the Viceroy of India and the British East India Company.
 
• The Indian independence movement, led by figures like Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru, and Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, aimed to end British rule and achieve self-governance.
 
• India gained independence from British rule on August 15, 1947, leading to the creation of the Dominion of India and the Dominion of Pakistan.

questions.question: ________ empowers the President to remove inconsistencies between laws passed by the Parliament and State Legislatures and the subjects included in the concurrent list.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 254**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 254 of the Indian Constitution deals with inconsistencies between laws made by the Parliament and laws made by the State Legislatures.
 
• It empowers the President to remove any inconsistency that may arise between laws passed by the Parliament and those passed by State Legislatures on subjects included in the Concurrent List.
 
• If there is a conflict between the central and state laws on a subject in the Concurrent List, the central law prevails over the state law.
 
• The President can give his/her assent to a state law that is inconsistent with a central law, after which the state law will prevail in that state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Concurrent List:**

 
 
• The Concurrent List is one of the three lists in the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution that outlines the subjects on which both the Parliament and State Legislatures can legislate.
 
• Some examples of subjects in the Concurrent List include criminal law, criminal procedure, marriage and divorce, bankruptcy and insolvency, and trusts and trustees.
 
 
 
• **Article 254(2):**
 
 
• Article 254(2) specifically allows a state law that is inconsistent with a central law to prevail in that state if it receives the President's assent.
 
• This provision ensures that the central government can maintain uniformity on certain subjects while still allowing states to enact laws that cater to their specific needs.
 
 
 
• **Seventh Schedule:**
 
 
• The Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution contains three lists: the Union List, the State List, and the Concurrent List.
 
• The Union List includes subjects on which only the Parliament can legislate, the State List includes subjects on which only the State Legislatures can legislate, and the Concurrent List includes subjects on which both can legislate.
 
 
 
• **Legislative Powers:**
 
 
• The distribution of legislative powers between the Parliament and State Legislatures is one of the key features of the Indian federal system.
 
• This distribution is intended to ensure that both levels of government can operate effectively within their respective domains.

questions.question: Sitara Devi was a dancer of the popular North Indian classical dance form __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kathak** is one of the eight major classical dance forms of India.
 
• It originated from the northern Indian states and is known for its intricate footwork and spins.
 
• Sitara Devi, often referred to as the "Queen of Kathak," was a renowned exponent of this dance form.
 
• Kathak is characterized by its storytelling aspect, often depicting tales from Indian epics like Mahabharata and Ramayana.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Manipuri:**

 
 
• Manipuri is another classical dance form of India that originated in the northeastern state of Manipur.
 
• It is known for its graceful and fluid movements, often depicting themes from the life of Lord Krishna.
 
 
 
• **Kathakali:**
 
 
• Kathakali is a classical dance-drama form from Kerala in southern India.
 
• It is known for its elaborate makeup, costumes, and face masks, as well as its intricate gestures and footwork.
 
 
 
• **Sattriya:**
 
 
• Sattriya is a classical dance form from Assam in northeastern India.
 
• It was introduced in the 15th century by the Vaishnavite saint Srimanta Sankardev as a part of his neo-Vaishnavism movement.
